structure: Seven selection-instruction shapes on one form: '(one box only)' over inline content-control boxes; 'Tick all that apply' over glyph boxes one per line; 'You may tick more than one box' over inline legacy boxes; '(select up to 3)' over content-control boxes one per line; a D28-like table whose box COLUMN is headed 'Select up to 3'; a D35-like blank medicines table with a 'Route (e.g., po)' column; and a D07-like ambiguous plural owner 'Recipient(s)' with no instruction.
authored_from: build_forms.py intent (f3_selection_instructions), written before any engine run on this form
slot_grammar: neutral v3 ground-truth grammar; see check_expected.py

body paragraphs b/p[5..8]: one printed ☐ glyph each, before its option word

areas.label: Services already involved.
areas.cardinality: any number, 0..4 ('You may tick more than one box')

printed_on_form.text: You may tick more than one box.

areas.label: Recipient(s) of this summary

destination.description: body paragraph b/p[21]: four printed ☐ glyphs on one line, each before its option words

areas.ambiguity: D07-like: the only cardinality evidence is the '(s)' of the owner label. The intended reading is multi-select (a summary can go to several recipients).
areas.grading_note: multi_choice = right. No field (held for the clinician) = safe, recorded as a usefulness loss. A single choice = wrong: it refuses a valid two-recipient answer (the D07 A20 failure).

areas.cardinality: one value; '(e.g., po)' is an example, never an option

medicines.must_never: a Route cell (or column) mapped as a choice whose options come from the example '(e.g., po)', or 'po' offered as a value

controls.printed: Goals for this admission (select up to 3)

destination.description: body paragraphs b/p[14..18]: one checkbox content control each, before its option words

controls.reason: The field contract has no selection limit. A multi_choice would accept four or five ticks against the printed rule; a single choice would refuse a legitimate two- or three-goal answer. The structural rule (V1-DECISIONS 2026-09-28) therefore HOLDS it for the clinician. This is a documented usefulness-loss control: holding is the expected outcome, not a defect.

destination.description: D28-like: table b/tbl[0], box column tc[1] under the header 'Select up to 3'; one printed ☐ glyph per row, the option words in column tc[0] of the same row

controls.reason: One limited selection spread over a column of per-row boxes. Mapping each row as an independent checkbox (or the column as an unlimited multi_choice) silently permits four or more ticks; the limit is unrepresentable, so the expected outcome is a hold. Documented usefulness-loss control, as f3.C1.
A printed column header with an example. It is neither a write-in nor a set of options.

destination.description: the box column's header cell in the D28-like table

controls.reason: A column header carrying the selection rule. It is not a write-in and not a question of its own words.

extras_policy: Any other answerable field (spacers b/p[3], b/p[9], b/p[12], b/p[19], b/p[22], trailing b/p[25], headings, header cells) is a false field.
